title: 2022年普通高等学校招生全国统一考试 英语听力（全国甲卷）
note: 2022年全国乙卷听力与本卷相同（甲乙卷共用同一套听力材料与音频，仅试卷其他部分不同）。听力原文取自天星教育 tesoon.com 在线听力页（Text 1—Text 10 完整原文），题干与选项、参考答案取自 21世纪教育网 zy.21cnjy.com 资源页《2022年全国甲卷高考英语试题（Word版含答案，含听力音频和原文）》，两处内容互相核对一致。第一节 5 段对话各 1 题，读一遍；第二节 5 段对话或独白共 15 题（2+2+3+4+4），读两遍。原文中用于标注答案线索的圈码（(6)(7) 等）已删除。

sections.name: 第一节
sections.desc: 听下面5段对话。每段对话后有一个小题，从题中所给的A、B、C三个选项中选出最佳选项。听完每段对话后，你都有10秒钟的时间来回答有关小题和阅读下一小题。每段对话仅读一遍。

materials.label: 第1段材料
materials.transcript:
M: Jenny, you can just drop me here.
W: But we're two streets away from the office.
M: It's fine. I had a big breakfast and feel like a bit of a walk.

questions.text: What does the man want to do?

materials.label: 第2段材料
materials.transcript:
W: Hello, George. You look tired. Didn't sleep well last night?
M: No, not at all. I had to work flat out to meet the project deadline. Now I'm really feeling a bit run-down.

questions.text: What was George doing last night?

materials.label: 第3段材料
materials.transcript:
W: John, can't we go someplace and talk? It's so noisy in here.
M: Well, there's a small park across the street. It's usually not crowded at this time of day.

questions.text: Why does the man suggest going to the park?

materials.label: 第4段材料
materials.transcript:
W: We've got to do something about the neighbor's dog.
M: Why? Has he been into your flower garden again?
W: The flower garden, the garbage can and yesterday he started digging holes in the yard.

questions.text: How does the woman sound?

materials.label: 第5段材料
materials.transcript:
M: Hello, we have a reservation in the name of Mr. Jones. Is there any table by the window?
W: Sorry, we've got this corner table for you. It's quiet here, not close to the door.

questions.text: Where is the man's table?

sections.name: 第二节
sections.desc: 听下面5段对话或独白。每段对话或独白后有几个小题，从题中所给的A、B、C三个选项中选出最佳选项。听每段对话或独白前，你将有时间阅读各个小题，每小题5秒钟；听完后，各小题将给出5秒钟的作答时间。每段对话或独白读两遍。

materials.label: 第6段材料
materials.transcript:
W: Dave, don't forget we're invited out to dinner tonight.
M: Oh, yeah. I almost forgot. What time?
W: 7:30. We should leave the house by 6:30. You know how bad the traffic is that time of night.
M: It's informal, isn't it?
W: Yeah. You can wear your new sports jacket. The one I got you as an anniversary gift.
M: OK. Well, I've got to go. I'll try to get home a little earlier today.
W: Good.

questions.text: What are the speakers going to do tonight?
What is the probable relationship between the speakers?

materials.label: 第7段材料
materials.transcript:
M: We need to decide exactly when we're going to move. Any suggestions?
W: I think July would be the best time. Our sales are always down that month. We could move all the office equipment at a weekend, do everything at once.
M: I think a weekend is too short. Maybe we should do it department by department.
W: What do you mean?
M: Well, each week, a different department would move. That way, there would always be people here to handle customer inquiries, phone calls and so on.
W: Hmm, that's a good idea.

questions.text: Why does the woman think July is the best time to move?
How will they handle the moving?

options.B: Have the sales section go first.
options.C: Do one department at a time.

materials.label: 第8段材料
materials.transcript:
W: So Mr. Peter Selz, I'd be curious to know what were the early connections in your life that led you into the art field.
M: My grandfather was an art dealer in Munich. They had a great museum in Munich. He took me to the museum, and I responded very strongly to what I saw on the walls there. I learned about art from him. I learned about looking at art from him. I think that's what really got me started. Then many years later, after I got out of the army, I went to study art history at the University of Chicago.
W: Tell us more about your experiences of looking at art with your grandfather.
M: Well, we looked at the famous paintings by the great artists like Rembrandt, Botticelli and Albrecht Durer. Rubens' paintings were my favorites. Yes, I remember these things. This was when I was between ten and fifteen. When I was fourteen, I was so anxious to see more art that a friend of mine and I bicycled across the Alps to see Venice. That was a big adventure.

questions.text: What did Peter learn from his grandfather?
What did Peter do in Chicago?
Whose works did Peter like best?

materials.label: 第9段材料
materials.transcript:
W: Hi, John. Haven't seen you for ages!
M: Hi, Susan. Fancy meeting you here on the train.
W: How is your college life?
M: What can I say? I've survived.
W: What happened?
M: Well, early last March, I started doing a part-time job in a law firm. A few weeks before, I had started writing my term paper. I thought I could finish it by August.
W: That was a pretty good idea, trying to have some work experience.
M: For the first three weeks, you know, I tried. I got up early and worked for an hour on my paper before going to work. But work was so fun. I met tons of new people, and soon I couldn't find even a minute for my paper. So I had to quit my part-time job, and finally finished my paper in October.
W: Well, it's never too late to mend. It's kind of hard to find a balance between what you have to do and what you want to do.
M: Yeah, it's really important for me to balance study and work. And I think I should learn to exercise some self-control.

questions.text: Where does the conversation take place?
By what time did John plan to finish his term paper?
Why did John quit his part-time job?

options.A: He had to catch up with his study.
options.B: He was offered a better one.

questions.text: What is Susan's attitude to John's problem?

materials.label: 第10段材料
materials.transcript: M: Being an athlete is very fun, painful and exciting. Every time I come to the track, I feel like I'm out of this place. This is Botswana National Stadium. This is where I train. When I saw Usain Bolt running in 2012 London Olympics, I was amazed. Just watching him run got me motivated. I quit being a chess player and started to run. I went to the 2016 Olympics and went to the finals at the age of 18. And wow, I finished 5th. It was a dream come true to me, but I still wanted more. The training is super hard, but the hardest part for me is that I got an injury, an injury which may take me out for years. For a period of time, as a young athlete, I didn't know what to do. I lost focus. But now, I'm back on the track. I really want to be there at the Olympics and do what I did before, do much, much greater. I don't care about the gold. I don't care about the silver. I want to do my best, you know, take everything and show it to the world.

questions.text: What did the speaker do before the year 2012?
Why was the 2016 Olympics important for the speaker?
Which is the hardest for the speaker?
What is the speaker mainly talking about?

options.A: His plan to go for the gold.
options.C: His love for his home country.
